title: European Stocks: Germany's DAX Rises for Third Straight Day; Yen Firm in 158 Range as Traders Adjust Positions Ahead of FOMC
text:

 Add preferred source European markets on the 28th saw stocks rise while the yen weakened and the euro strengthened in currency trading. The dollar-yen stood at 158.15 yen, and the euro-yen at 176.30 yen. Germany's DAX rose 113.25 points to 25,704.02, its third consecutive gain, while the UK's FTSE 100 also edged higher. Trading was dominated by position adjustments ahead of policy decisions from the FOMC and the ECB. The Bank of Canada raised its policy rate by 0.25% to 2.50%, its first rate hike in three years and three months. Germany's November consumer confidence index deteriorated to minus 30.8. Key Elements 
 Germany Stock Index (DAX) FTSE 100 Index Bank of Canada (BOC) US Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) European Central Bank (ECB) dollar-yen exchange rate euro-dollar exchange rate Deutsche Bank Siemens Energy National Grid BP German Consumer Confidence Index (GfK survey) European financial markets on the 28th saw stocks broadly higher, while the foreign exchange market saw the yen weaken and the euro strengthen. With the US Federal Open Market Committee's (FOMC) announcement of its decision and Fed Chair Warsh's press conference scheduled for the following day, trading was dominated by position adjustments among market participants.
 In the currency market, the dollar-yen stood at 158.15 yen per dollar, 0.33 yen weaker for the yen and stronger for the dollar compared with 3:00 p.m. the previous day. After briefly falling to 157.65 yen in the evening Japan time, buying regained the upper hand once the previous day's low of 157.42 yen was seen as near-term support. Amid rising US long-term interest rates, yen selling and dollar buying intensified, and just before 1:00 a.m. the pair hit 158.25 yen, a fresh intraday high. Market participants noted that "the upper limit of the Ichimoku cloud at 158.44 yen and the 200-day moving average at 158.54 yen are being watched as upside resistance levels."
 The euro-dollar was at 1.1148 dollars per euro, a slight gain for the euro and decline for the dollar. Euro selling led early amid uncertainty over the Middle East situation, and in the evening the pair touched 1.1113 dollars, matching the year-to-date low marked on the 14th, but it was bought back after selling ran its course. Just before 2:00 a.m. it hit 1.1153 dollars, an intraday high. The euro-yen stood at 176.30 yen per euro, 0.83 yen weaker for the yen and stronger for the euro, and shortly after 1:30 a.m. it reached 176.40 yen, the day's high.

 Euro-dollar 1.1148 dollars 0.0030 dollar stronger for euro

 Note: △ indicates a plus, ▲ indicates a minus. Bond yields move inversely to prices.
 In the stock market, London's FTSE 100 Index rebounded slightly. Selling for position adjustment led as major companies' earnings reports got into full swing, but the index later turned higher, lacking clear direction. Utility stocks such as National Grid and SSE were bought, and energy stocks including BP and Shell also rose. On the other hand, pharmaceutical stocks such as GSK were sold.
 Frankfurt's DAX rose for a third consecutive session, closing at 25,704.02, up 113.25 points from the previous trading day. Buying emerged on the back of gains in Asian stock markets including Japan and South Korea, but the advance was capped by position-adjustment selling ahead of the FOMC and the European Central Bank's (ECB) regular policy meeting the following day. Among individual stocks, Deutsche Bank rose 3.97%, Siemens Energy gained 3.64%, and Siemens Healthineers climbed 1.72%, posting notable gains.
 In European bond markets, UK government bonds rose (yields fell), while German government bonds fell (yields rose).
 Among European economic indicators released on the day, Germany's November consumer confidence index (GfK survey) came in at minus 30.8, deteriorating from the previously announced minus 30.6.
 In North America, the Bank of Canada (BOC, Canada's central bank) decided to raise its policy rate by 0.25% to 2.50%. The hike was the first since July 2023, three years and three months ago. The statement pointed to the risk of prolonged inflation stemming from the Middle East situation and indicated a stance of "proceeding cautiously given the existence of uncertainty, while further policy rate increases may prove necessary." The dollar-Canadian dollar traded in a range between the lower and mid-1.40 Canadian dollar levels.
 Market participants showed a strong inclination to wait and see the FOMC's announcement and Chair Warsh's press conference, with comments that "position-adjustment moves are dominating." The direction of US long-term interest rates is expected to continue to influence the direction of the dollar-yen exchange rate.
 The resilience of European stocks was largely supported by improved risk appetite from higher Asian equities and inflows into utility and energy stocks. However, with policy decisions from two major central banks—the FOMC and the ECB—scheduled on consecutive days, aggressive buying to chase higher prices was limited. In the currency market, the dollar-yen continued a top-heavy pattern in the lower 158 yen range, and whether it can break through the resistance band from 158.44 yen to 158.54 yen will be the near-term focus. The euro-dollar also continued to trade near its year-to-date low range, and the policy message from the ECB's governing council meeting could determine the market's direction.
